certificate.title: Module 5: Using AI to Build Applications, Tools & Dashboards Completion

course.description: Capstone module. Use AI as your builder — describe what you need in plain language and watch it create working tools, dashboards, and calculators. No coding required. Build your capstone portfolio piece and complete your collection of five working AI agents.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Module 5: Using AI to Build Applications, Tools & Dashboards.

modules.description: What AI is good at: building things. How AI changes the tool-building equation for finance teams — from months-long IT requests to 30-minute prototypes. The full range of what you can build.

activities.title: What AI Is Good At: Building Things

lessons.content:
This one surprises people the most. AI can build functional software — applications, tools, dashboards, calculators, trackers — from a plain-language description. You describe what you want, and AI writes the code, creates the interface, and makes it work.

You don't need to be a developer. You don't need to understand code. You just need to know what problem you're solving and what the output should look like.
lessons.title: What AI Is Good At: Building Things

lessons.content:
Think about how tools get built in most finance organizations:

| Traditional Approach | AI Approach |
|---------------------|-------------|
| Identify a need → Submit a request to IT → Wait 3-6 months → Maybe get what you asked for | Identify a need → Describe it to AI → Have a working prototype in 30 minutes |
| Need a developer for anything beyond Excel | AI is your developer — available 24/7 |
| Custom tools cost thousands of dollars | AI builds them for the cost of your subscription |
| You get what IT interprets from your requirements | You get what you described — and you can iterate instantly |

This isn't about replacing IT or building enterprise systems. It's about solving the smaller problems that never make it to the top of IT's backlog — the departmental tools, the team dashboards, the calculators, the trackers. The things you currently solve with increasingly complex spreadsheets.
lessons.title: How This Changes Things

lessons.content:
The range is wider than you'd expect:

**Calculators and Models**
- Lease classification calculator (ASC 842)
- Depreciation schedules
- Loan amortization tables
- Bonus/commission calculators
- Tax estimation tools

**Dashboards and Visualizations**
- Budget vs. actual dashboards
- Cash flow forecasting visualizers
- Close progress trackers
- KPI dashboards
- Headcount and compensation summaries

**Trackers and Management Tools**
- Open items trackers
- Audit request managers
- Contract renewal trackers
- Vendor payment status boards
- Team task boards for close cycle

**Data Tools**
- Data format converters
- Reconciliation matchers
- Report generators
- Comparison tools (period over period, entity over entity)
- Consolidation helpers
lessons.title: What You Can Build

lessons.content:
Pick something you wish existed in your work — a tool, a calculator, a tracker, a dashboard, or a simple application. The best candidates are things where you currently use spreadsheets, manual tracking, or workarounds because no one has built the "real" solution.

**The default example used throughout this module is:**

> **A budget vs. actual dashboard** — a live, interactive view that shows spending against budget by department, highlights variances, and lets you drill into the details.

If you're not sure what to pick, use this default. Otherwise, choose your own build and follow along with the same steps.

**Note on building:** Some AI platforms have built-in capabilities for creating interactive artifacts (Claude can create React components, ChatGPT can run Python code and create files). For this module, Claude's **artifact** feature is particularly useful because it lets AI build interactive web applications right in the conversation. But any platform will work — AI can also generate code you save and run locally, or create Excel-based tools.
lessons.title: Choose Your Build

modules.title: Context / Theory

modules.description: Hands-on steps. Describe a tool to AI, have it build it, iterate on the design, add real data, build a second tool, share for feedback, and reflect.

lessons.content:
Go to one of the platforms listed above and sign in.

- **ChatGPT** → https://chat.openai.com
- **Claude** → https://claude.ai (recommended for this module — the artifact feature lets you build interactive tools right in the conversation)
- **Grok** → https://grok.com
lessons.title: Step 1: Open an AI Tool

activities.title: Step 2: Describe What You Want to Build

lessons.content:
Tell AI what you need. Be specific about:
- **What problem it solves** — what are you trying to do?
- **Who uses it** — just you, your team, stakeholders?
- **What it should show** — what does the output look like?
- **What data goes in** — what inputs does it need?

> **Try this (default example):**
> "Build me an interactive budget vs. actual dashboard. Here's what I need:
>
> - It should show spending by department against their budget
> - I want to see the variance in both dollars and percentage
> - Color-code it: green if under budget, yellow if within 5%, red if over 5%
> - Let me click on a department to see the line-item detail
> - Include a summary bar at the top showing total company budget vs. actual
> - Use sample data for 6 departments and 5-6 expense categories each
> - Make it look professional — this is something I'd show to leadership
>
> I want this to be a working, interactive tool — not just a static table."

Hit enter and watch AI build it. If you're using Claude, it will create an interactive artifact you can click, explore, and use right there. If you're using another platform, it will generate code you can run.
lessons.title: Step 2: Describe What You Want to Build

lessons.content:
Your first version is a prototype. Now make it better — the same way you refined writing in Module 2. Just tell AI what to change:

**Example follow-ups:**

| You Say | What Happens |
|---------|-------------|
| "Add a chart — a bar chart showing each department's budget vs. actual side by side" | AI adds a visual chart |
| "Add a filter so I can look at one quarter at a time" | AI adds interactive filtering |
| "The colors are too bright — use a more corporate color scheme" | AI adjusts the design |
| "Can you add a trend line showing how variance has changed month over month?" | AI adds historical trending |
| "Add an export button so I can download this data as CSV" | AI adds export functionality |
| "Make the numbers formatted with dollar signs and commas" | AI formats the display |
| "Add a section that shows the top 3 departments most over budget" | AI adds a highlight section |

Each iteration makes the tool more useful. And because AI builds instantly, you can try things out and change your mind — something that's impossible when you're waiting on IT.
lessons.title: Step 3: Iterate on the Design

lessons.content:
Once you're happy with the design, replace the sample data with your actual numbers:

> "This looks great. Now I'm going to replace the sample data with my actual budget and actual figures. Here's the data: [paste your data]"

Or, if you want to keep the tool flexible:

> "Instead of hardcoded data, can you add an upload feature where I can paste or upload a CSV with my budget and actual figures each month? I want to reuse this tool without editing the code."

Now you have a working tool with your real data. This is something you can use in your next budget review meeting.
lessons.title: Step 4: Add Your Real Data

lessons.content:
Now that you've built one thing, build another. Pick something different to see the range of what's possible:

**A close progress tracker:**
> "Build me a close progress tracker. I need to track 25 close tasks — each with a task name, owner, due date, status (not started / in progress / complete), and a progress bar showing overall completion. Let me click to update status. Show a timeline view of what's due each day of close."

**A loan amortization calculator:**
> "Build me a loan amortization calculator. Inputs: principal, interest rate, term in months, start date. Output: full amortization schedule showing each payment broken into principal and interest, running balance, and cumulative interest paid. Add a chart showing the principal vs. interest breakdown over time."

**A vendor scorecard:**
> "Build me a vendor evaluation scorecard. I want to score vendors across 5 categories: pricing, quality, timeliness, communication, and compliance. Each category gets a 1-5 rating. Show an overall weighted score with a visual radar chart. Let me save and compare multiple vendors."

**A data format converter:**
> "Build me a tool where I can paste data in one format (like a bank statement CSV) and it converts it to a different format (like our GL import template). Let me define the column mapping and save it for reuse."
lessons.title: Step 5: Build Something Else

lessons.content:
If you built something useful, show it to a colleague. Ask them:
- Does this solve the problem you expected?
- What's missing?
- What would make it more useful?

Then go back to AI and iterate based on their feedback. This is exactly how professional software development works — build, share, get feedback, improve. The difference is that your iteration cycle is minutes, not weeks.
lessons.title: Step 6: Share and Get Feedback

lessons.content:
You just used AI to build functional tools. Think about the experience:

- What was the hardest part — knowing what to build, describing it to AI, or refining the output?
- How does the tool compare to what you would have done in Excel?
- Could you see using this tool in your actual work? What would need to change?
- What other tools or dashboards would make your team more effective?

This is a fundamentally new capability for finance professionals. The ability to describe a tool in plain language and have it built in minutes means that the bottleneck is no longer "who will build it" — it's "what should we build?" And the answer to that question is something you, as the finance expert, are best positioned to know.
lessons.title: Step 7: Reflect

modules.title: Now To Do

modules.description: Every area of the finance function where AI can build tools — management reporting, financial planning, operations dashboards, team tools, and personal productivity.

lessons.content:
- **Executive dashboards:** Build interactive dashboards that leadership can explore — budget performance, headcount trends, cash positions, revenue metrics. Better than static PowerPoint slides, faster than waiting for a BI team.

- **Flash reports:** Automated flash reports that update when you drop in new numbers. No more copying and pasting into a formatted template every month.

- **Board-ready visualizations:** Professional charts and visual summaries that look polished enough for a board meeting — without design skills.
lessons.title: Management and Reporting

lessons.content:
- **Scenario modeling tools:** Build tools that let you adjust assumptions (revenue growth rate, headcount changes, FX rates) and immediately see the impact on the forecast. Interactive what-if analysis.

- **Capital budgeting calculators:** NPV, IRR, payback period calculators with sensitivity tables and visual outputs. Give leadership an interactive tool instead of a static spreadsheet.

- **Cash flow forecasting:** A tool that takes your receivables, payables, and planned activities and projects cash position forward — with adjustable timing assumptions.
lessons.title: Financial Planning

lessons.content:
- **Close management dashboard:** Track every close task, its status, owner, and timeline. See at a glance what's on track and what's behind.

- **Audit management tracker:** Track PBC requests, status, who's responsible, and due dates. Share a live view with the audit team instead of sending status emails.

- **Contract management tool:** Track contract terms, renewal dates, auto-renewal windows, and value. Get alerts when action dates are approaching.
lessons.title: Operations and Process

lessons.content:
- **Onboarding guides:** Interactive onboarding tools for new team members — click through processes, systems, and key contacts.

- **Knowledge bases:** Build a searchable tool where your team's process documentation, policies, and FAQs live in one place.

- **Training applications:** Simple tools that help team members practice calculations, test their understanding of standards, or walk through procedures.
lessons.title: Team Tools

lessons.content:
- **Task prioritizers:** Input your to-do list and have AI help you sort by urgency, impact, and dependencies.

- **Meeting prep tools:** Input an agenda and key topics, and have AI generate a prep sheet with talking points, relevant data, and questions to raise.

- **Personal finance calculators:** Mortgage comparison tools, investment return calculators, tax estimation tools — build anything you'd normally search for online but want customized to your situation.
lessons.title: Personal Productivity

modules.title: Application

modules.description: Optional capstone. Polish your best build to portfolio-ready quality, save it, create a builder agent, and complete your five-agent training portfolio.

lessons.content:
*This section is optional. It takes the basic skill you just learned — using AI to build tools — and turns it into a capstone portfolio piece: your own custom-built tool or dashboard, documented and shareable.*

In the main exercise, you built tools within an AI conversation. That's powerful — but the tools live inside that conversation. To make your builds truly useful and shareable, you can save them, document them, and add them to your portfolio.

This is your capstone piece. It's the most tangible artifact in your portfolio — something you built with AI that solves a real problem.
lessons.title: The Idea

lessons.content: A **polished tool, dashboard, or application** that you've refined, documented, and saved to your portfolio. This is the one you'd show someone if they asked "what can you do with AI?"
lessons.title: What You'll Create

lessons.content: Look back at the tools you built in this module. Which one is the most useful? Which one solves a real problem in your work? That's your capstone piece. If none of them feel right, build something new — this time with the intention of making it portfolio-ready.
lessons.title: Step 1: Pick Your Best Build

lessons.content:
Take your chosen tool and refine it to a professional standard:

> "I want to polish this dashboard to be portfolio-ready. Please:
> 1. Clean up the design — make it look professional and consistent
> 2. Add a title and brief description of what it does
> 3. Make sure all the features work smoothly
> 4. Add clear labels and formatting for all numbers
> 5. Include a simple instructions section so someone else could use it"
lessons.title: Step 2: Polish It

activities.title: Step 3: Save It to Your Portfolio

lessons.content:
**Option A: Save locally.** If AI generated code (HTML, Python, etc.), save the file to your computer. Create a folder called "AI Portfolio" and keep your builds organized there.

**Option B: Save in ChatGPT, Claude, or Grok.** Keep the conversation where you built the tool — name it clearly so you can find it again. In ChatGPT, you can save it as a GPT. In Claude, you can keep it in a project.

**Option C: Create an agent for it in AI Gym.**

1. Open the **AI Gym** app and sign in (if not yet downloaded: https://aigym.studio/#download) — you'll land on the **Home** page (your Hub agent)
2. On Home, type: *"Create an agent called [Your Tool Name] Builder in my My Training Portfolio org with these instructions:"* and paste the instructions below
3. The Hub creates it for you. Or go to the **Org** page → My Training Portfolio → **+ New Agent**
4. **Name:** `[Your Tool Name] Builder` — for example, `Budget Dashboard Builder`
5. **Instructions:** Give it instructions that describe the tool and how to recreate or update it:

```
You are a tool builder agent that creates and maintains my [Budget vs. Actual Dashboard / whatever you built].

This tool:
- [Describe what it does]
- [Describe the inputs it needs]
- [Describe the outputs it produces]

When I ask you to build or update this tool:
- Use the same design and format as the original
- Accept new data and generate an updated version
- Maintain the professional look and feel
- Add any new features I request

Here's the original design specification: [paste the description you used to create it]
```

The Hub creates the agent for you. Alternatively, go to the **Org** page → My Training Portfolio → **+ New Agent** and paste the instructions there.
lessons.title: Step 3: Save It to Your Portfolio

lessons.content:
Go to the **Home** page and chat with your **Using AI Series Agent** to give it your final update:

> "I just completed Module 5 — the final module. I built a [tool name] using AI. It [describe what it does]. I also created a builder agent so I can recreate and update it anytime. My complete portfolio now includes:
> - Module 1: Research agent for learning topics deeply
> - Module 2: Communications writer for drafting professional messages
> - Module 3: Review analyst for checking documents and data
> - Module 4: Process optimizer for improving manual tasks
> - Module 5: [Tool name] builder for creating and maintaining custom tools
>
> The biggest thing I learned across all five modules was [your reflection]."
lessons.title: Build on Your Portfolio

lessons.content:
You now have a **complete training portfolio** with five working agents and a capstone tool:

| Module | Agent / Artifact | What It Does |
|--------|-----------------|-------------|
| 0 | Using AI Series Agent | Tracks your portfolio and connects your learning |
| 1 | Research Expert | Deep research on any topic, on demand |
| 2 | Communications Writer | Professional writing, tailored to your voice |
| 3 | Review Analyst | Critical review of documents, data, and work products |
| 4 | Process Optimizer | Finds and implements efficiency improvements |
| 5 | Custom Tool Builder | Builds and maintains tools, dashboards, and applications |

This isn't a certificate. It's a set of working AI tools you built yourself — tools you can use in your job starting tomorrow. And you know how to build more.
lessons.title: What You've Built

modules.title: Bonus: Going Deeper

modules.description: Key terms introduced in this module, explained in plain language.

lessons.content: In AI platforms like Claude, an artifact is an interactive output — like a web application, a chart, or a tool — that AI creates right in the conversation. You can click, interact with, and download artifacts. Think of it as AI building something functional, not just text.
lessons.title: Artifact

lessons.content: A first version of a tool or application. AI excels at rapid prototyping — building a working first version in minutes that you can test, get feedback on, and iterate. The prototype isn't final, but it's functional enough to validate the idea.
lessons.title: Prototype

lessons.content: Building software without writing code yourself. When AI builds a tool from your plain-language description, that's essentially no-code development. You describe, AI builds. The code exists — AI wrote it — but you didn't need to touch it.
lessons.title: Low-Code / No-Code

lessons.content: An interactive visual display of key metrics and data. Dashboards let you see the big picture at a glance and drill into details as needed. AI can build dashboards from data you provide — with charts, filters, color-coding, and interactive elements.
lessons.title: Dashboard

lessons.content: The cycle of build → test → improve → repeat. With AI, this cycle takes minutes instead of weeks. You build a first version, see what works, tell AI what to change, and get an improved version immediately. This is how professional software development works — AI just makes it accessible to everyone.
lessons.title: Iteration / Rapid Prototyping

lessons.content: Saving the output of an AI-built tool in a format you can use elsewhere — CSV files, HTML files, PDF reports, or code you can run independently. Export lets your AI-built tools integrate with the rest of your workflow.
lessons.title: Export
